for_you_if: you enjoy open world shooters with cooperative campaigns
you can overlook intrusive story missions interrupting exploration
not_for_you_if: you will not install the required third party launcher
you want unhindered exploration without forced interruptions
you expect a responsive cooperative progression system

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks settings to turn off camera head bob, causing motion sickness.

citations.review_text:
This will be quick. Have had this game in my library for a long time, and finally installed it. Loved the look when I started it up, and was really looking forward to playing it. About 15 minutes later I was already dizzy, and I realized it has a camera head bob. And no settings or even mods I could find to turn it off.

Look, I understand and can even appreciate the desire to make the game as real as possible. But one, I personally don't think it's necessary. The world does not bounce around my eyes like mad as I walk or run. Even in games where it doesn't make me want to vomit, I find it super annoying. And two, and mostly two, why in the world would you want to exclude a bunch of potential players by not putting in an option to turn the bob off? It's just stupid. And in a bazillion hours of gaming I've only found about two other games that have hit me with motion sickness. And none as quickly as this one did.

14 minutes in I was thinking about getting Far Cry 6. 15 minutes in Far Cry 5 is uninstalled and permanently removed from my library, so no sales on 6 after all. So nice job on the janky camera.

I have never play a Far Cry game before, and heard FC5 has good immersion and visuals for a Montana setting, and on sale for $13, my only worry was that it won't work well enough. But, my machine seems to run it very smoothly, even if my display is a cheap TV locked to 30 fps. Gunplay is a little lacking (no hit indications, visual or audio). And requiring Ubisoft Connect is mildly annoying. But Overall, excited to get into it!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world and missions as repetitive.

citations.review_text: The first 10 hours is very fun and well made but the game gets repetitive fast with the other areas being much more empty than the first, very little gun selection and the same tasks over and over

Oh my, this is a really terrible game. I'm serious. I don't mean to hate, but it's so bad.
I don't really play "AAA" games anymore, it's been some years now, but I had time recently and this was in my library for a while, probably from a Humble Bundle because I don't remember ever purchasing this, and I thought "why not, this will for sure not be revolutionary but at least it will be some high-budget polished fun". IT'S NOT. AT ALL. I've played Far Cry from 1 to 4, and enjoyed them for their merits, even if each was progressively less good than the previous one, they were still pleasant to play, so I though "how bad can this one be", oh my...
The fact it's sitting at 80% recommendation at the time of this review is baffling to me. How bad can the rest of UbiSoft games have become after this one for so many people to consider this as a good game?!

It's crazy how it can have so many cutscenes that prevent me from playing, and at the same time have almost no story whatsoever. I have a vague clue of what's going on, but nothing really makes sense, no character does, everything is forgettable, and it's not like it's an interesting sandbox: the map is large and empty at the same time. You're bombarded with tons of things to do, but this is just "content", uninteresting, repeating, "bad-mmo-go-kill-me-10-wolves" type of content. I kid you not, In the first hour of playing I already had a quest to kill 3 bears. In 30 min, I must have seen more than 10 times the same van with a prisoner go by so I could release him, over and over again.
There's no friction anywhere when it comes to gameplay, everything is made to be as easy as possible, not to frustrate even a child, which is, funny enough, very frustrating. There's no stakes, you're just supposed to have fun rolling on everything and just check the list of the 3 types of activities there is to do (basically, besides boring and uninspired story missions, it's destroy some crap, free some prisoners and liberate a camp), repe…

The game feels mediocre. You can mod the gun you start with but there is little to no incentive to use other weapons or to really progress that way. The missions and enemies feel a bit repetitive. The story starts alright but there are some scenes that make no sense and feel way too forced. This game had a lot of potential but it feels a bit like slop

claims.claim: Progression relies on a resistance system that periodically interrupts open-world exploration by forcibly kidnapping the player into mandatory story cutscenes.

citations.review_text:
English:
Far Cry 5 has a great Montana atmosphere but the game constantly throwing cultists at you and forcing you into story missions completely ruins the exploration. Being kidnapped out of nowhere while just walking around the map is extremely annoying and makes the experience feel suffocating. Leveling up is quite easy but because you are constantly interrupted it is hard to enjoy the open world. I played it solo and just wanted to explore in peace without being dragged into missions by force.

Türkçe:
Far Cry 5 aslında harika bir Montana atmosferine sahip ama oyunun sürekli üzerinize tarikatçı fırlatması ve sizi zorla ana görevlere çekmesi keşif hissini tamamen mahvediyor. Haritada gezerken durduk yere kaçırılmak inanılmaz sinir bozucu ve deneyimi gerçekten boğucu bir hale getiriyor. Karakteri kasmak oldukça kolay ama sürekli bölündüğünüz için açık dünyanın tadını çıkaramıyorsunuz. Tek başıma oynadım ve sadece kafamı dinleyerek etrafı gezmek istemiştim ama oyun buna pek izin vermedi.

The open world, vehicles, gunplay, fantastic, plot is cool, but the way they throw you into cutscenes is super annoying. like you'll be flying a chopper and all of a sudden you have been abducted? and it happens like 20 times as you progress. BUT! the grass, trees, water, landscape, glorious!

This is a solo game, not a multiplayer one. Solo wise it's ok. The multiplayer is not, you are a hostage to whoever is the host of the session, also the achievements are mostly in solo. Anyway buy it only if you plan to play it solo. 

My second and last complain is the forced interaction with the enemies when you reach certain milestones. I would like the opportunity to ressist, which i did a lot of times. Some times fighting for 30 to 40 minutes until randomly i am taken.

I was 50-50 to give it a thumbs up or thumbs down. I would prefer to give it a "neutral" rating. The gameplay loop is quite fun. Open world, nice rural area, it feels like playing GTA but in first person. There are main missions, side missions, extra activities to do, random NPCs to talk, random enemies you meet as you travel the area. It is easy to go around following markers and the map, to do everything you want of these and in any order.
The reason I gave it thumbs down is the main story and how it unfolds. There are 4 main villains in total and when the time comes to interact with them, cutscenes trigger where you are captured and taken to them and you can not do nothing about it. One time you feel like a terminator destroying your enemies and the next you feel like a trapped kid that can do nothing but wait for his NPC friends to save him. Very annoying. Also, the main story's ending felt really disappointing and is the main reason I give it thumbs down, although the open world gameplay was good and fun. The ending left me so frustrated that now I do not even want to log in again to finish all the quests and activities I have left and I will just uninstall and move to another game.

The quintessential modern Ubisoft game - a plot that is mediocre at best and overflowing with plot holes, glitchy gameplay, and annoying mechanics. Half the cinematics running on less than 15 FPS is also on par.

The open world gameplay loop is decent enough, so of course they added a forced kidnapping mechanic to make sure you can't even enjoy that.

Gunplay is okay, but that is offset by vehicles having awful controls and helicopters being insanely overpowered (other than the fact that you can still somehow be kidnapped while flying in one high above the ground).

Graphics are fairly good and game runs reasonably smooth (outside of cinematics).

[h1] Far Cry 5 – When You Just Want to Go Fishing but End Up Toppling a Cult [/h1]

I put [b]37 hours[/b] into this game, and somehow I managed to liberate an entire county, catch fish, hunt wildlife, fly planes, accidentally blow up my companions... and realize that Montana is probably the least peaceful place on Earth.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] A World That Never Gets Boring [/h2]

Far Cry 5's biggest strength is its open world.

It's beautiful, alive, and completely unpredictable. You leave an outpost thinking you're finally heading to your next mission, then suddenly there's a firefight on the road. You deal with that, a plane starts shooting at you. You shoot the plane down, a bear appears out of nowhere. You survive the bear... only to be greeted by a cultist carrying a flamethrower.

At some point, this just becomes your average Tuesday.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Pure Far Cry Chaos [/h2]

The game gives you plenty of freedom. You can clear outposts, hunt, fish, explore, or simply drive around enjoying the scenery.

The Guns for Hire system is also fantastic.

Boomer can spot enemies better than most scouts, Hurk believes every problem can be solved with a rocket launcher (and usually creates two more), and Cheeseburger...

Well, he's a bear.

That's all the explanation anyone should need.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Not Everything Is Perfect [/h2]

The resistance system can get annoying.

Sometimes you're peacefully fishing or collecting herbs when the game suddenly decides:
[i]"Nope. You're getting kidnapped. The story isn't going to progress itself."[/i]

Some missions feel repetitive, and the enemy AI occasionally makes you wonder how this cult managed to survive for so long.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] The Atmosphere [/h2]

The soundtrack is incredible.

The cult's choir songs are so good that you almost forget the people singing them are about to shoot you on sight.

Joseph Seed and his family are memorable villains, and each one has their own uni…

Karakteri kasmak oldukça kolay ama sürekli bölündüğünüz için açık dünyanın tadını çıkaramıyorsunuz. Tek başıma oynadım ve sadece kafamı dinleyerek etrafı gezmek istemiştim ama oyun buna pek izin vermedi.

The open world, vehicles, gunplay, fantastic, plot is cool, but the way they throw you into cutscenes is super annoying. like you'll be flying a chopper and all of a sudden you have been abducted? and it happens like 20 times as you progress. BUT! the grass, trees, water, landscape, glorious!

I was 50-50 to give it a thumbs up or thumbs down. I would prefer to give it a "neutral" rating. The gameplay loop is quite fun. Open world, nice rural area, it feels like playing GTA but in first person. There are main missions, side missions, extra activities to do, random NPCs to talk, random enemies you meet as you travel the area. It is easy to go around following markers and the map, to do everything you want of these and in any order.
The reason I gave it thumbs down is the main story and how it unfolds. There are 4 main villains in total and when the time comes to interact with them, cutscenes trigger where you are captured and taken to them and you can not do nothing about it. One time you feel like a terminator destroying your enemies and the next you feel like a trapped kid that can do nothing but wait for his NPC friends to save him. Very annoying. Also, the main story's ending felt really disappointing and is the main reason I give it thumbs down, although the open world gameplay was good and fun. The ending left me so frustrated that now I do not even want to log in again to finish all the quests and activities I have left and I will just uninstall and move to another game.

[h1] Far Cry 5 – When You Just Want to Go Fishing but End Up Toppling a Cult [/h1]

I put [b]37 hours[/b] into this game, and somehow I managed to liberate an entire county, catch fish, hunt wildlife, fly planes, accidentally blow up my companions... and realize that Montana is probably the least peaceful place on Earth.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] A World That Never Gets Boring [/h2]

Far Cry 5's biggest strength is its open world.

It's beautiful, alive, and completely unpredictable. You leave an outpost thinking you're finally heading to your next mission, then suddenly there's a firefight on the road. You deal with that, a plane starts shooting at you. You shoot the plane down, a bear appears out of nowhere. You survive the bear... only to be greeted by a cultist carrying a flamethrower.

At some point, this just becomes your average Tuesday.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Pure Far Cry Chaos [/h2]

The game gives you plenty of freedom. You can clear outposts, hunt, fish, explore, or simply drive around enjoying the scenery.

The Guns for Hire system is also fantastic.

Boomer can spot enemies better than most scouts, Hurk believes every problem can be solved with a rocket launcher (and usually creates two more), and Cheeseburger...

Well, he's a bear.

That's all the explanation anyone should need.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Not Everything Is Perfect [/h2]

The resistance system can get annoying.

Sometimes you're peacefully fishing or collecting herbs when the game suddenly decides:
[i]"Nope. You're getting kidnapped. The story isn't going to progress itself."[/i]

Some missions feel repetitive, and the enemy AI occasionally makes you wonder how this cult managed to survive for so long.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] The Atmosphere [/h2]

The soundtrack is incredible.

The cult's choir songs are so good that you almost forget the people singing them are about to shoot you on sight.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the main character as completely silent, which detracts from emotional connection and immersion during the story.

citations.review_text:
The breathtaking landscapes of Hope County to the unforgettable soundtrack and intense gameplay, Far Cry 5 delivers an amazing open-world experience. The freedom to explore, cause chaos, and approach missions however you like makes every play session enjoyable. 
My only small complaint is that the main character is silent, which made it a bit harder to connect with them. Other than that, it's easily one of the best open-world games I've played.

9/10 – A true masterpiece

Far Cry 5 was, is, and always will be an incredible game.
After almost 50 hours of playing, finishing the main story, and completing both DLCs, its time to right a review.

Main game

Pros:
-The story is neat with the whole Eden's Gate cult thing going on, and the ending was well done.
-The main character is unvoiced, which I find more immersive than as in Far Cry 4.
-There are loads of guns to choose from, most are from previous games, but some are new.
-Joseph Seed (The main villain) was very well done, in a mysterious/creepy kind of way.
-Most of the other characters are done ok. Hurk is always a laugh, and I thought Nick Rye was cool.
-The outfit system was a cool feature, which I'm glad to have heard made it into Far Cry 6.

Cons:
-Some of the achievements are stupidly hard like kill 5,000 zombies. Like, who decided that would be fun?! And to add to it, I hate it when you have achievements for multiplayer stuff, and that stuff is gonna shut down one day (If it isn't already, I haven't checked).
-I wish the game was longer, or had some story after the ending, or a DLC that takes place right after. Now I am aware of Far Cry New Dawn, which actually takes place like 20 years after or something, but I've heard that game is crap anyways, so Ubisoft did try.

Hours Of Darkness DLC
Pros:
-The setting is excellent in Vietnam, during the Vietnam War.
-For a short story, it was it was a fun adventure that shows what its like surviving in the middle of a war-zone.
-Your companions can actually die, like forever die, which I found to be more immersive.
-Your companions have unique personalities that can make things just a little more interesting.

Cons:
-After a while, as in most Far Cry games, the fear of the enemy fades away after a while, they are less of a challenge.

Lost On Mars DLC

Pros:
-Mars was an unexpected yet interesting setting.
-Guns are cool, and I had fun using them.
-Hurk was funny, and his little "side mission" we'll call it, was hilarious, yet tedious.…

[h2] Far Cry 5 is the game that perfected the Far Cry formula[/h2]

I know there are plenty of people who will tell you that Far Cry 3 is the peak of the franchise. Nostalgia is a powerful thing.

After playing almost every major Far Cry game back-to-back, I don't agree.

One thing I will say before talking about the game itself... Ubisoft Connect is still an absolute disaster. Having to use a VPN just to launch the game, being told my password was wrong, then being told I couldn't reuse my old password, followed by "invalid password" despite meeting every requirement, before finally being locked out for "too many attempts"... yeah, not exactly the best first impression.
Thankfully, once you're actually in the game, things get a lot better.


[h2]The Good[/h2]


The biggest improvement for me is simply how polished the overall gameplay feels. Vehicle controls have finally been updated to use RT/LT on a controller instead of the strange left-stick acceleration from previous games, combat feels weightier than ever thanks to excellent weapon sound design, and Hope County is an absolute joy to explore.

The soundtrack deserves special mention. Somehow Ubisoft managed to combine country music with church hymns and choir pieces into something that fits the atmosphere perfectly. By the final hour of the game, the music elevates several scenes into some of the most memorable moments in the series.

Hope County itself is also the best open world Ubisoft has created for a Far Cry game. It's huge, but it never feels empty. Between the roads, helicopters, planes, random encounters and entertaining side missions, I constantly found myself getting distracted. Normally in open-world games I'm someone who rushes the main story, but here I actually wanted to clear side content because it was so enjoyable. Missions like helping bulls "romance" cows while Marvin Gaye's Sexual Healing plays in the background perfectly sum up just how random and memorable some of them a…
